title: Albumin–globulin interaction fails to improve transferred handgrip prediction beyond flexible conventional measures
abstract: We tested whether a sex-specific albumin-by-globulin interaction adds physiological predictive information beyond flexible additive proteins and conventional body-size measures. Models trained in NHANES2011–2012 (n=3916) were frozen and tested in separately recruited2013–2014 (n=4412). Target MEC-weighted mean squared error increased from 128.6851 to 129.8770kg², delta +1.1920; joint source/target rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.2825,+2.7351]. The registered improvement criterion failed. Adding the interaction to a comparator that also includes a flexible albumin/globulin ratio likewise did not improve point error. This exploratory negative result is specific to concurrent grip prediction and two recruitment cohorts in one survey program; it does not establish absence of protein-related biological information.
